name: The New Horde
summary: In the Valley of Trials, Eitrigg calls the Horde's newest recruits to the Den. He sends you to Gornek for training and explains why he returned to the Horde and what Thrall hopes it can become.

sections.title: A Veteran's Return
sections.body: Under Warchief Thrall's orders, Eitrigg watches over the newest hopefuls in the Valley of Trials. After the Second War, he left the Old Horde, sickened by its corruption under the Burning Legion. He lived in quiet exile until humans captured him. Thrall rescued Eitrigg, and the veteran returned when he learned of the young Warchief's dream: an honorable Horde rooted in ancestral shamanism and free of demonic masters.

sections.title: Reporting to the Den
sections.body: Before you leave the Valley of Trials' harsh canyons, Eitrigg sends you to the shaded cavern called the Den to speak with Gornek. Gornek speaks plainly about how rough new aspirants are. He watches over their training so only those who master discipline and survival reach the wider lands of Durotar.

faq.answer: Eitrigg is an aging orc veteran who saw the Old Horde fall under the Burning Legion's corruption. Disillusioned, he withdrew into quiet exile in Lordaeron. Humans captured him, and Thrall later freed him. Eitrigg pledged himself to Thrall's reformed Horde and now helps train recruits in the Valley of Trials.

faq.q: Why does Eitrigg talk about the 'New Horde'?
aliases: difference between old and new horde
faq.answer: The original Horde fell under demonic bloodlust and the Burning Legion's influence. Thrall's New Horde rejected demonic control, restored the old shamanic ways, and sought an honorable, independent future for orcs and their allies in Kalimdor.
Gornek waits just inside the Den's entrance, in a prominent cave cut into the Valley of Trials' northern rock wall.

faq.q: What happens after reporting to Gornek?
aliases: next quest after the new horde
faq.answer: After you report to Gornek, he accepts you as one of Eitrigg's trainees and gives you your first field assignments. You defend the valley and prove you are ready to serve the Horde.
Eitrigg left the Horde in disgust at its demonic corruption and the senseless slaughter driven by warlocks serving the Burning Legion during the earlier wars.

faq.q: Why are recruits trained in the Valley of Trials?
aliases: purpose of the valley of trials
faq.answer: The Valley of Trials gives young orcs and allied newcomers a secluded, rugged place in Durotar to face dangerous beasts and scorpids under veteran trainers' watch before they set out into the wider world.

angles.text: For the Horde, Thrall's rule means a break from demonic servitude and a return to honor, survival, and ancestral identity.
As an orc entering the Valley of Trials, you meet Eitrigg, who remembers your people's tragic past and its redemption under Thrall.
As a Darkspear troll, you train alongside the orcs in the Valley of Trials and share Thrall's vision of survival and honor.
